_meta.title: REBNY RLS + Trestle Master Field Registry
sources: data/rebny-rls-property-fields.csv (902 REBNY IDX Plus fields across 7 resources)

trestleArchitecture.description: Documents how REBNY RLS fields are accessed via the Trestle API. Three distinct mechanisms exist.

1_PropertyEntity.description: Standard RESO fields on the Trestle Property entity. Accessed directly via OData $select.

2_CustomPropertyEntity.description: Extension fields on Trestle's CustomProperty entity. Requires $expand=CustomProperty in the API call. Contains both named typed columns (AdditionalFee*) and a CustomFields JSON blob (MaxLength 100000).
2_CustomPropertyEntity.customFieldsBlob: CustomFields (Edm.String, MaxLength=100000) — JSON blob where REBNY-specific fields may be stored

3_BuildingLevelSplit.description: REBNY defines separate building-level fields (e.g., BuildingHeating) that do NOT exist as typed Trestle fields. Instead, Trestle implements building-level values as Building*-prefixed enum members within parent fields (e.g., Heating enum includes BuildingCitySteam, BuildingElectric). Consumer must parse and split these from unit-level values.

4_RebnyCustomFields.description: ~10 fields defined by REBNY that have NO equivalent on Trestle's Property or CustomProperty typed schema. These were created by REBNY and hosted on the Trestle platform. Likely accessed via the CustomFields JSON blob on CustomProperty entity. Requires verification with live API calls.
4_RebnyCustomFields.nycContext: These fields exist because NYC real estate has unique concepts (doorman types, co-op board rules, flip tax, rent stabilization, UCBA co-broke terms) not found in national RESO standard.

knownCsvErrors.issue: REBNY CSV maps abbreviation 'Mews' to value 'Meadows'. Mews is a distinct NYC street suffix (Washington Mews, Sniffen Court Mews). Meadows does not exist as a NYC street suffix.

Value 'ResidenManagerFullTime' — likely typo, missing 't' (should be 'ResidentManagerFullTime'). Registry preserves CSV value exactly. Column C uses 'BuildingStaff' while Column F uses 'BuildingStaffType' — name mismatch in CSV.

BathroomsFull.rebnyDescription: A room containing all 4 of the 4 elements constituting a bath, which are; Toilet, Sink, Bathtub or Shower Head. A Full Bath will typically contain four elements; Sink, Toilet, Tub and Shower Head (in tub or stall). However, some may considered a Sink, Toilet and Tub (without a shower) a Full Bath, others consider this to be a Three Quarter Bath. In the event that BathroomsThreeQuarter is not in use, this field may represent the sum of all Full and Three Quarter bathrooms.
BathroomsFull.label: FULL BTHS

BathroomsHalf.rebnyDescription: A room containing 2 of the 4 elements constituting a bath, which are; Toilet, Sink, Bathtub or Shower Head. A Half Bath will typically contain a Sink and Toilet.

BathroomsOneQuarter.rebnyDescription: A room containing 1 of the 4 elements constituting a bath which are; Toilet, Sink, Bathtub or Shower Head. Examples are a vanity with a sink or a WC (Water Closet, which is a room with only a toilet).

BathroomsPartial.rebnyDescription: The number of partial bathrooms in the property being sold/leased. When used in combination with the BathroomsFull field, this replaces (or is the sum of) all Half and One Quarter bathrooms; and in the event BathroomsThreeQuarter is not used, BathroomsFull replaces (or is the sum of) all Full and Three Quarter baths. This field should not be used in combination with the BathroomsOneQuarter or the BathroomsHalf.

BathroomsThreeQuarter.rebnyDescription: A room containing 3 of the 4 elements constituting a bath, which are; Toilet, Sink, Bathtub or Shower Head. A typical Three Quarter Bath will contain Sink, Toilet and Shower. Some may considered a Sink, Toilet and Tub (without a shower) a Three Quarter Bath, others consider this to be a Full Bath.

BathroomsTotal.rebnyDescription: Sum of the number of bathrooms with half baths expressed as a decimal.

BathroomsTotalInteger.rebnyDescription: The simple sum of the number of bathrooms. For example for a property with two Full Bathrooms and one Half Bathroom, the Bathrooms Total Integer will be 3. Expressing this example as 2.5, you will need to use a non-standard field name. Decimal based bathrooms are not recommended but possible via the Dictionary's extensibility.

CoListAgentFullName.rebnyDescription: The full name of the co-listing agent as registered with DOS Licensing

CoListAgentURL.rebnyDescription: The website URL of the co-listing agent.

ComingSoonTimestamp.rebnyDescription: The transactional timestamp automatically recorded by the RLS system representing the date/time the listing first entered the Coming Soon status.

CommercialUnitsYN.rebnyDescription: Indicates the building contains commercial units. Commercial units are exclusively for business-related purposes or to provide a workspace rather than as a living space, which would instead constitute residential real estate.

CommonInterest.rebnyDescription:
Common Interest is a type of ownership in a property that is composed of an individual lot or unit and a share of the ownership or use of common areas. A Common Interest Development (CID) is usually governed by a recorded set of Covenants, Conditions & Restrictions (CC&Rs).
This will be used to indicate Condominium, Stock Cooperative, Condop, RentalBuilding, or None.
CommonInterest.label: OWNERSHIP
CommonInterest.complianceNotes: Must NOT cross-match (Co-op must not match Condo or Condop). Rental adds 'Rental Building'.

Concessions.rebnyDescription: Are there concessions included in the sales/lease agreement? Yes, No or Call Listing Agent

ConcessionsAmount.rebnyDescription:
The dollar amount of the concessions. If the concessions are made by the seller, some may subtract this value from the sales price as a means of calculating their own true price. If concessions are made by the buyer, some may add this amount to the sale price to create their own true price. Concessions made by both buyer and seller should be subtracted from each other providing a net value. Details of this calculation should be added to the Concessions Comments field.

ConcessionsAmount can also be used for listings that are for lease/rent to indicate whether there are bonus or discount/reduction amount towards rent, deposit, etc

ConcessionsBuyerBrokerFee.rebnyDescription: The dollar amount of the concession agreed upon at closing for the buyer broker fee.  Accepted for Closed status listings only.
ConcessionsBuyerBrokerFee.conditionalRule: No; Data entered only when MLSStatus is changed to Closed

ConcessionsClosingCosts.rebnyDescription: The dollar amount of the concession agreed upon at closing for the closing costs.
ConcessionsClosingCosts.conditionalRule: No; Data entered only when MLSStatus is changed to Closed

ConcessionsComments.rebnyDescription: Comments describing the concessions made by the buyer or the seller/landlord.

ConcessionsOtherCosts.rebnyDescription: The dollar amount of the concession agreed upon at closing for the other costs.  Accepted for Closed status listings only.
ConcessionsOtherCosts.conditionalRule: No; Data entered only when MLSStatus is changed to Closed

ConcessionsPropertyImprovementCosts.rebnyDescription: The dollar amount of the concession agreed upon at closing for the property improvements. Accepted for Closed status listings only.
ConcessionsPropertyImprovementCosts.conditionalRule: No; Data entered only when MLSStatus is changed to Closed

ConstructionMaterials.rebnyDescription: A list of the materials that were used in the construction of the property.

Cooling.rebnyDescription: A list describing the cooling or air conditioning features of the property.

CoolingYN.rebnyDescription: The property has cooling or Air Conditioning.

CoOwnershipInterest.rebnyDescription: Describe the interest or shares in which the listing is for. This should be fractional or percentage.

CoOwnershipRemarks.rebnyDescription: Describe the co-ownership, the usage, or limitations/restrictions

Country.rebnyDescription: The country abbreviation in a postal address.
Country.conditionalRule: If submitted the value must be US

CountyOrParish.rebnyDescription: The County, Parish or other regional authority
CountyOrParish.conditionalRule:
; CityRegion must match with CountyOrParish:
Kings-Brooklyn
Queens- Queens
New York- Manhattan
Richmond- Staten Island
Bronx-Bronx
CountyOrParish.label: BOROUGH
CountyOrParish.complianceNotes: Used for borough-level filtering. Maps to CountyOrParish in RESO.

CrossStreet.rebnyDescription: Nearest cross streets to the property. This field is in addition to, and independent of, the driving directions field.
CrossStreet.label: CROSS ST

CumulativeDaysOnMarket.rebnyDescription: The number of days the property is on market, as defined by the RLS business rules.
CumulativeDaysOnMarket.label: CDOM

CurrentPrice.rebnyDescription: The current price of the listing. CurrentPrice = ListPrice for all statuses except for Closed. CurrentPrice = ClosePrice for closed listings.

CurrentUse.rebnyDescription:
A list of the type(s) of current use of the listing that is for sale or lease within the residential building. The current use of the property is an important factor in understanding the overall condition of the listing and determining its appropriateness for intended use.
This is not to be used to identify any commercial listings.

DaysOnMarket.rebnyDescription: The number of days the listing is on market, as defined by the RLS business rules. Please refer to the UCBA to make the appropriate calculation for DaysOnMarket.
DaysOnMarket.label: DOM

DeliveredVacantYN.rebnyDescription: Will the property be delivered vacant?

DepositAmount.rebnyDescription: The security deposit the tenant/buyer must pay to the landlord/seller, expressed as a dollar amount.

DevelopmentStatus.rebnyDescription: A list of the Development Status of the property. The developmental status of land is an important factor in selling, purchasing and developing of land properties.

DiningType.rebnyDescription: The property's primary type of dining.

DirectionFaces.rebnyDescription: The compass direction that the main entrance to the building faces. For example, North, South, East, West, South-West, etc. It may also be known as the building exposure.

DocumentsAvailable.rebnyDescription: A list of the Documents available for the property. Knowing what documents are available for the property is valuable information.

DocumentsChangeTimestamp.rebnyDescription: System generated timestamp of when the last update or change to the documents for this listing was made.

DocumentsCount.rebnyDescription: The total number of documents or supplements included with the listings.

DoorFeatures.rebnyDescription: A list of features or description of the doors included in the sale/lease.

DuplicateListingIDs.rebnyDescription: Only to be used if the property have two listings submitted for the purpose of  1) Coexclusive  2) Property is listed both for sale and lease

Electric.rebnyDescription: A list of electric-service related features of the property (e.g. 110 Volt, 3 Phase, 220 Volt, RV Hookup). Note: the previous "Electric" field was renamed to DistanceToElectricComments

ElectricExpense.rebnyDescription: The annual expense that is not paid directly by the tenant and is included in the Operating Expense calculations.

ElectricOnPropertyYN.rebnyDescription: Does the property currently have electrical utility available on the property.

ElevatorsTotal.rebnyDescription: Number of elevators in the building. If there is no elevator then enter '0'. If ElevatorsTotal is greater than 0 then BuildingFeatures to have Elevator(s) as value.

EntryLevel.rebnyDescription: A numeric field that describes the level within the structure, SFR or a unit in a building, where the main entry to the dwelling is located. Entry Level is not used for the unit but for the building in which the property is located.
EntryLevel.label: FLOOR

Exclusions.rebnyDescription: Elements of the property that will not be included in the sale. i.e. Chandeliers will be removed prior to close.

ExpirationDate.rebnyDescription: The date when the listing agreement will expire. This is the date entered by the agent reflecting when the change occurred, or will occur, contractually, not a timestamp of when the change was made in the MLS. The expiration date of listings, prior to their expiration, cancellation, sale or lease, is confidential information and should be restricted to the agent and their managers, partners or broker.
ExpirationDate.conditionalRule: ; The ExpirationDate entered can be a maximum of 10 years from the current date. Any ExpirationDate more than 10 years in the future will be rejected.

Exposures.rebnyDescription: All cardinal direction exposures of the listing that is for sale/lease
Exposures.label: EXPOSURES

ExteriorFeatures.rebnyDescription: A list of features or description of the exterior of the property included in the sale/lease. (For Building specific, refer to the BuildingExteriorFeatures)

Fencing.rebnyDescription: A list of types of fencing found at the property being sold.

FireplaceFeatures.rebnyDescription: A list of features or description of the fireplace(s) included in the sale/lease.
FireplaceFeatures.conditionalRule: If FireplaceYN = true OR if FireplaceTotal > 0

FireplacesTotal.rebnyDescription: The total number of fireplaces included in the listing.
FireplacesTotal.conditionalRule: Must be greater than 0 if FireplacesYN = true

FireplaceYN.rebnyDescription: Does the property include a fireplace.

FlipTax.rebnyDescription: The flip tax or transfer fee to be paid for this sale/lease, expressed as either a percentage or a constant currency amount.
FlipTax.conditionalRule: If CommonInterest = Condominium, StockCooperative, or Condoop AND PropertyType = Residential

FlipTaxRemarks.rebnyDescription: A text description of the flip tax or transfer fee to be paid for this sale/lease.

FlipTaxType.rebnyDescription: A list of types to clarify the value entered in the FlipTax field. For example $, % or some other clarification of the FlipTax.
FlipTaxType.trestleAccessMethod: REBNY-custom field. NOT on Trestle Property or CustomProperty typed columns. Defined by REBNY, hosted by Trestle. Likely accessed via CustomFields JSON blob on CustomProperty entity ($expand=CustomProperty). Requires verification with live API call.

Flooring.rebnyDescription: A list of the type(s) of flooring found within the listing.

FloorNumber.rebnyDescription: Floor number of unit (or main entrance to unit if unit duplex/unit triplex/etc.)

FoundationArea.rebnyDescription: The area or dimensions of the footprint of the structure on the lot.

FoundationDetails.rebnyDescription: A list of the type(s) of foundation on which the property sits.

FractionalUnitNumber.rebnyDescription: Unit Number Plus Weeks Assigned (For Example 501-Week 52)

FuelExpense.rebnyDescription: The annual expense that is not paid directly by the tenant and is included in the Operating Expense calculations.

Furnished.rebnyDescription: The listing being leased is furnished, unfurnished or partially furnished.

FurnishedListPrice.rebnyDescription: The current price of the listing when furnishings are included. Depending on the listing, this may or may not be equal to the list price.
FurnishedListPrice.conditionalRule: If Furnished = Furnished OR Partially OR Negotiable

FurnishedMaxLeaseMonths.rebnyDescription: The maximum length of the lease when furnished, expressed as a number of months.
FurnishedMaxLeaseMonths.conditionalRule: If Furnished = Furnished OR Partially OR Negotiable

FurnishedMinLeaseMonths.rebnyDescription: The minimum length of the lease when furnished, expressed as a number of months.
FurnishedMinLeaseMonths.conditionalRule: If Furnished = Furnished OR Partially OR Negotiable

GarageSpaces.rebnyDescription: The number of spaces in the garage assigned or part of the listing that is for sale/lease.

GarageSpacesAssignedYN.rebnyDescription: Indicate whether the unit or listing has a designated parking assigned or included in the sale/lease.

GarageYN.rebnyDescription: A flag indicating that the property/building has garage space.

GardenerExpense.rebnyDescription: The annual expense that is not paid directly by the tenant and is included in the Operating Expense calculations.

GreenBuildingVerificationType.rebnyDescription: The name of the verification or certification awarded to a new or pre-existing residential or commercial structure. For example: LEED, Energy Star, ICC-700. In cases where more than one certification have been awarded, leverage multiple iterations of the green verification fields via the repeating element method.

GreenBuildingYN.rebnyDescription: A building has been certified as green in which  design, construction or operation, reduces or eliminates negative impacts, and can create positive impacts, on our climate and natural environment.

GreenEnergyEfficient.rebnyDescription: Pick list of general green attributes such as energy efficient doors, or appliances without naming specific elements with ratings that may wane over time.

GreenEnergyGeneration.rebnyDescription: Methods of generating power that are included in the sale or lease.

GreenIndoorAirQuality.rebnyDescription: Pick list of indoor air quality measures without naming specific elements with ratings that may wane over time.

GreenLocation.rebnyDescription: Pick list describing efficiencies involved with the property's location such as walkability or transportation proximity without naming specific elements with ratings that may wane over time.

GreenSustainability.rebnyDescription: Pick list of sustainable elements used in the construction of the structure without naming specific elements with ratings that may wane over time.

GreenWaterConservation.rebnyDescription: Pick list of general water conserving attributes of the property such as landscaping or reclamation without naming specific elements with ratings that may wane over time.

GuarantorsAcceptedYN.rebnyDescription: Indicate whether a guarantor is accepted on listing/unit level. Refer to the buildingrules for building policies.

Heating.rebnyDescription: A list describing the heating features of the property.

HeatingYN.rebnyDescription: Indicates whether or not the property has heating.

HomeWarrantyYN.rebnyDescription: Indicates whether or not a home warranty is included in the sale of the property.

IDXEntireListingDisplayYN.rebnyDescription: If this is True and the ListOfficeIDXParticipationYN is True, then the listing can be sent to an IDX website.
IDXEntireListingDisplayYN.conditionalRule: : The LMPs are required to set this attribute to default as True.

Inclusions.rebnyDescription: Portable elements of the property that will be included in the sale.

InsuranceExpense.rebnyDescription: The annual expense that is not paid directly by the tenant and is included in the Operating Expense calculations.

InteriorFeatures.rebnyDescription: A list of features or description of the interior of the property included in the sale/lease.

InternetAddressDisplayYN.rebnyDescription: A yes/no field that states the seller has allowed the listing address to be displayed on Internet sites.
InternetAddressDisplayYN.complianceNotes: COMPLIANCE GATE: If false, show 'Address Available Upon Request' instead of actual address.

InternetAutomatedValuationDisplayYN.rebnyDescription: A yes/no field that states the seller allows the listing can be displayed with an AVM on Internet sites.

InternetConsumerCommentYN.rebnyDescription: A yes/no field that states the seller allows a comment or blog system to be attached to the listing on Internet sites.

InternetEntireListingDisplayYN.rebnyDescription:
A yes/no field that states the seller has allowed the listing address to be displayed on Internet sites.

Sale listings with Permissions=Null are not allowed to submit InternetEntireListingDisplayYN=False.  

Listing alerts and auto-sharing must be disabled/turned off for any non-exclusive agent’s listings when InternetEntireListingDisplayYN = False

If Internet Entire Listing Display YN = False, Matrix will automatically override and set the below fields to False:

•        Internet Address Display YN = False

•        Internet Consumer Comment YN = False

KitchenCondition.rebnyDescription: General condition of the property's kitchen(s).
KitchenCondition.trestleAccessMethod: REBNY-custom field. NOT on Trestle Property or CustomProperty typed columns. Defined by REBNY, hosted by Trestle. Likely accessed via CustomFields JSON blob on CustomProperty entity ($expand=CustomProperty). Requires verification with live API call.

LaborInformation.rebnyDescription: Information about labor laws that are applicable to the building. i.e. Union, Non-Union, Employee License Required.

LandAssessedValue.rebnyDescription: Assessed value of the land only.

LandLeaseAmount.rebnyDescription: When the land is not included in the sale, but is leased, the amount of the lease. This is the Space Rent for Mobile homes in a Park.

LandLeaseAmountFrequency.rebnyDescription: When the land is not included in the sale, but is leased, the frequency the Land Lease Fee is paid.

LandLeaseExpirationDate.rebnyDescription: When the land is not included in the sale, but is leased, the expiration date of the Land Lease.

LandLeaseYN.rebnyDescription: The land is not included in the sale and a lease exists.

LandmarkStatusYN.rebnyDescription: Indicates whether a property has been designated landmark status by the government. Having some sort of historic, artistic, or aesthetic value.

Latitude.rebnyDescription: The geographic latitude of some reference point on the property, specified in degrees and decimal parts. Positive numbers must not include the plus symbol.
Latitude.label: LAT
Latitude.complianceNotes: Used for map view and transit/commute tool.

LaundryFeatures.rebnyDescription: Add this pick list of features and locations where the laundry is located in the property being sold/leased. Refer to BuildingLaundryFeatures for building specific details.
LaundryFeatures.label: W/D

LeaseRenewalOptionYN.rebnyDescription: Indicates whether or not there is an option to renew the lease for the listing.

LeaseType.rebnyDescription: The lease type. Options are Stabilized lease and Non-stabilized lease.
LeaseType.conditionalRule: If PropertyType = ResidentialLease AND CommonInterest = RentalBuilding
LeaseType.trestleAccessMethod: REBNY-custom field. NOT on Trestle Property or CustomProperty typed columns. Defined by REBNY, hosted by Trestle. Likely accessed via CustomFields JSON blob on CustomProperty entity ($expand=CustomProperty). Requires verification with live API call.

LegalRoomsTotal.rebnyDescription: The number of legal rooms in the building.

Levels.rebnyDescription: The number of levels in the property being sold/leased. For example, One Level, Two Levels, Three or More Levels, Multi/Split, Loft. A discreet horizontal plane of interior living space (excluding basements).

LicensesExpense.rebnyDescription: The annual expense that is not paid directly by the tenant and is included in the Operating Expense calculations.

ListAgentDirectPhone.rebnyDescription: North American 10 digit phone numbers should be in the format of ###-###-#### (separated by hyphens). Other conventions should use the common local standard. International numbers should be preceded by a plus symbol.
ListAgentDirectPhone.label: AGENT PHONE

ListAgentEmail.rebnyDescription: The email address of the Listing Agent.
ListAgentEmail.label: AGENT EMAIL

ListAgentFullName.rebnyDescription: The full name of the list agent as registered with DOS Licensing
ListAgentFullName.label: AGENT
ListAgentFullName.complianceNotes: Per-listing attribution required on print/email. NEVER include in description field.

ListAgentHasOwnershipInterestYN.rebnyDescription: Indicates if list agent or list broker have ownership interest of the listing.

ListAgentKeyNumeric.rebnyDescription: Unique identifier of the List Agent. This is the foreign key that relates to the Member resource MemberKeyNumeric

ListAgentMlsId.rebnyDescription: The local, well-known identifier for the member. This value may not be unique, specifically in the case of aggregation systems, this value should be the identifier from the original system.

ListAgentNickname.rebnyDescription: The Alternate name used by the List Agent

ListAgentStateLicense.rebnyDescription: The license of the listing agent. Separate multiple licenses with a comma and space.

ListAgentURL.rebnyDescription: The website URL of the listing agent.

ListingAgreement.rebnyDescription: The nature of the agreement between the seller and the listing agent. Examples are Exclusive Agency, Open Listing, CoExclusive, etc. Please note: Per UCBA, RLS comprises of all exclusive listings. Please reference the UCBA for further details.
ListingAgreement.conditionalRule: - If PropertyType = Residential, then cannot submit Exclusive Right To Lease. If PropertyType = Residential Lease, then cannot submit Exclusive Right to Sell.
ListingAgreement.label: LISTING TYPE

ListingContractDate.rebnyDescription:
The effective date of the agreement between the seller landlord and the seller's broker. This is the date entered by the agent reflecting when the change occurred contractually, not a timestamp of when the change was made in the RLS. 

This date is not editable once submitted.
ListingContractDate.conditionalRule: ; ListingContractDate cannot be more than one year from current date.

ListingID.rebnyDescription: The local, well-known identifier for the Listing. This value may not be unique, specifically in the case of aggregation systems, this value should be the identifier from the original system.
ListingID.conditionalRule: No, generated by Matrix DB with ID for RLS/REBNY

ListingIssues.rebnyDescription: This field specifies an issue with the listing that requires restrictions and/or corrections

ListingKeyNumeric.rebnyDescription: The unique identifier for the listing.

ListingSocialMediaURL.rebnyDescription: The URL for social media related to this listing.

ListingTerms.rebnyDescription: Terms of the listing such as Lien Release, Subject to Court Approval or Owner Will Carry. Also may include options that describe the financing terms that are acceptable to the seller, i.e. cash, assumable, FHA loan, etc.

ListingURL.rebnyDescription: Provides a link to the specific listing on a brokerage website, agent website or other public-facing source.

ListOfficeIDXParticipationYN.rebnyDescription: Does the List Office/Broker participate in IDX? True value allows the listing to be sent to an IDX (provided that the list office participates in IDX). This is generated from the IDXOfficeParticipationYN attribute in Member resource and managed through the REBNY membership directory.

ListOfficeKeyNumeric.rebnyDescription: Unique identifier of the List Office. This is the foreign key that relates to the Office resource OfficeKeyNumeric

ListOfficeMlsId.rebnyDescription: The local, well-known identifier. This value may not be unique, specifically in the case of aggregation systems, this value should be the identifier from the original system.

ListOfficeName.rebnyDescription: The legal name of the brokerage representing the seller.
ListOfficeName.label: COMPANY

ListOfficePhone.rebnyDescription: North American 10 digit phone numbers should be in the format of ###-###-#### (separated by hyphens). Other conventions should use the common local standard. International numbers should be preceded by a plus symbol.

ListOfficeURL.rebnyDescription: The website URL for the listing office.

ListPrice.rebnyDescription:
The current price of the property as determined by the seller/landlord. For auctions this is the minimum or reserve price.
For rent/leasing, it must reflect the the gross monthly rent/lease for the listing (not net-effective rent).
ListPrice.label: PRICE
ListPrice.complianceNotes: Sale = total price in dollars. Rental = monthly rent. Filter IDs: saleMinPrice/saleMaxPrice, rentalMinRent/rentalMaxRent

ListTeamKeyNumeric.rebnyDescription: Unique identifier of the List Team. This is the foreign key that relates to the Team resource TeamKeyNumeric

ListTeamMlsId.rebnyDescription: The local, well-known identifier. This value may not be unique, specifically in the case of aggregation systems, this value should be the identifier from the original system.

ListTeamName.rebnyDescription: The name of the team representing the seller/landlord

LivingArea.rebnyDescription: The total livable area within the structure of the unit or property in which it is for sale or lease.
LivingArea.conditionalRule: If PropertyType = Residential AND CommonInterest = Condominium
LivingArea.label: INT SQFT
LivingArea.complianceNotes: Can be null. Filter must skip null values. Filter IDs: saleMinSqft/saleMaxSqft, rentalMinSqft/rentalMaxSqft

LivingAreaSource.rebnyDescription: The source of the measurements. This is a pick list of options showing the source of the measurement (e.g., Agent, Assessor, Estimate).

LivingAreaUnits.rebnyDescription: A pick list of the unit of measurement for the area. i.e. Square Feet, Square Meters, Acres, etc.

Longitude.rebnyDescription: The geographic longitude of some reference point on the property, specified in degrees and decimal parts. Positive numbers must not include the plus symbol.
Longitude.label: LNG
Longitude.complianceNotes: Used for map view and transit/commute tool.

LotFeatures.rebnyDescription: A list of features or description of the lot included in the sale/lease.

LotSizeArea.rebnyDescription: The total area of the lot. See Lot Size Units for the units of measurement (Square Feet, Square Meters, Acres, etc.).
LotSizeArea.conditionalRule: PropertySubType = any of Single Family Townhouse, Duplex, MIxed Use, Multi Family, Multi Family Townhouse, Quadruplex, Single Family Residence, Triplex, Unimproved Land

LotSizeDimensions.rebnyDescription: The dimensions of the lot minimally represented as length and width (i.e. 250 x 180) or a measurement of all sides of the polygon representing the property lines of the property. i.e. 30 x 50 x 120 x 60 x 22.
LotSizeDimensions.conditionalRule: PropertySubType = any of Single Family Townhouse, Duplex, MIxed Use, Multi Family, Multi Family Townhouse, Quadruplex, Single Family Residence, Triplex, Unimproved Land

LotSizeSource.rebnyDescription: The source of the measurements. This may be a pick list of options showing the source of the measurement. i.e. Agent, Assessor, Estimate, etc.

LotSizeUnits.rebnyDescription: A pick list of the unit of measurement for the area. i.e. Square Feet, Square Meters, Acres, etc.

MaintenanceExpense.rebnyDescription: The annual expense that is not paid directly by the tenant and is included in the Operating Expense calculations.

MajorChangeTimestamp.rebnyDescription: Timestamp of the last major change on the listing (see also MajorChangeType).

MajorChangeType.rebnyDescription: Description of the last major change on the listing, i.e. “price reduction”, “back on market”, etc. May be used to display on a summary view of listing results to quickly identify listings that have had major changes recently.

ManagerExpense.rebnyDescription: The annual expense that is not paid directly by the tenant and is included in the Operating Expense calculations. This is for an individual manager. Use ProfessionalManagementExpense for a management company.

ManagingAgencyListingYN.rebnyDescription: This field distinguishes between a listing that is handled directly by an owner or an owner’s Managing Agency (having signed up with REBNY), versus a listing that is handled through a standard real estate brokerage company.

MatrixTesting.rebnyDescription: Flag to identify whether it is a test listing submitted. This will be automatically flagged for the LMPs as they are currently testing.  This flag will not be available once migrated to production

MaximumFinancingAmount.rebnyDescription: The maximum amount a lender will finance for the listing, expressed as an amount.

MaximumFinancingPercent.rebnyDescription: The maximum amount a lender will finance for the listing, expressed as a percentage of the sale price.
MaximumFinancingPercent.conditionalRule: PropertyType = Residential AND CommonInterest = Condominium, StockCooperative, or Condop

MaximumFinancingRemarks.rebnyDescription: Text description of the maximum allowed financing.
MaximumFinancingRemarks.conditionalRule: PropertyType = Residential AND CommonInterest = Condominium, StockCooperative, or Condop

MaxLeaseMonths.rebnyDescription: The maximum length of the lease expressed as a number of months.

MinLeaseMonths.rebnyDescription: The minimum length of the lease expressed as a number of months.
MinLeaseMonths.conditionalRule: If PropertyType = ResidentialLease. The value must be greater than or equal to 1

MlsMajorChangeType.rebnyDescription: Description of the last MLS status major change on the listing, i.e. “price reduction”, “back on market”, etc. May be used to display on a summary view of listing results to quickly identify listings that have had major changes recently.

MlsStatus.rebnyDescription: RLS Status. Each MlsStatus maps to a single StandardStatus. Multiple MlsStatus may map to a single StandardStatus.

ModificationTimestamp.rebnyDescription: The transactional timestamp automatically recorded by the RLS system representing the date/time the listing was last modified.
ModificationTimestamp.label: UPDATED
ModificationTimestamp.complianceNotes: Required on every listing output per REBNY compliance.

MoveInCosts.rebnyDescription: Specific fees not included in the base rent or deposit that apply to the listing (e.g., application fees, move-in fees).

MoveInCostsComments.rebnyDescription: Comments or clarifications regarding the additional listing fees.Comments or clarifications regarding the Move In Costs.

MoveInCostsAmountTotal.rebnyDescription: The total monetary value of all Move In Costs associated with the listing.

NetMonthlyRent.rebnyDescription: The lease monthly amount a lessee pays on average per month of a lease period, a mathematical calculation that takes into account free months on the lease as if they'd been paid for.

NewConstructionYN.rebnyDescription: Indicates whether or not the property is newly constructed and has not been previously occupied.

NewDevelopmentYN.rebnyDescription: Indicates whether or not the property with a structure(s) that is(are) newly constructed, converted or both selling individual units.
NewDevelopmentYN.conditionalRule: but cannot enter NewDevelopmentYN = True on Coming Soon listings

NewlyConvertedUnitYN.rebnyDescription: Indicate whether the unit was newly converted from rental or any other property type to condo/coop.

NewTaxesExpense.rebnyDescription: The annual expense that is not paid directly by the tenant and is included in the Operating Expense calculations.

NumberOfBuildings.rebnyDescription: Total number of separate buildings on the premise.

NumberOfProfessionalUnitsTotal.rebnyDescription: Total number of professional units in building.

NumberOfRetailUnits.rebnyDescription: Total number of retail units in building.

NumberOfSeparateElectricMeters.rebnyDescription: Total number of separate meters included/part of the listing.

NumberOfSeparateGasMeters.rebnyDescription: Total number of separate meters  included/part of the listing.

NumberOfSeparateWaterMeters.rebnyDescription: Total number of separate meters  included/part of the listing.

NumberOfShares.rebnyDescription: The number of shares allocated to the specific listing.
NumberOfShares.conditionalRule: If PropertyType = Residential AND CommonInterest = StockCooperative OR Condops

NumberOfUnitsInCommunity.rebnyDescription: The total number of units in the building, complex or community. This is not the number of units being sold, but rather the size of the community in which the dwelling being sold is located.

NumberOfUnitsTotal.rebnyDescription: Total number of residential units included in the property, occupied or unoccupied.

NumberOfUnitsVacant.rebnyDescription: The number of units currently vacant.

OccupantType.rebnyDescription: A field that describes the type of occupant, i.e. Owner, Tenant, Vacant.

values.description: The unit is ADA compliant.

A minimum of one entrance to the structure with a clear, evenly paved walkway from a parking or pedestrian arrival area. The path of travel does not include a running slope in excess of 1:12 (8.33%), a cross slope exceeding 1:50 (2%), nor level changes of more than 1/2". If slope is over 5%, handrails are required. Level landing; 32" clear width opening doors and adequate lighting on pathway and landing. This is required to be considered "visitable."

Bedroom has adequate turnaround of 60" or other approved turnaround configuration. Closet doors have 32" clearance. Accessible environmental controls and multiple lighting fixtures. This is required to be considered Enhanced Accessible. Optional: Some lower-height storage in closet. Remote control of lighting and environmental controls.

Hard surface flooring or low-pile carpet, securely attached along edges. Entrances to all rooms on all floors provide 36" clear passage. Multiple lighting fixtures installed to provide adaptable lighting for general purpose and tasks. This is required to be considered Enhanced Accessible.
Closet doors are 32” clearance throughout the central living area.
Common area, used for entertaining guests, level, with 36" passage through and around the space. Required to be considered Visitable.
Minimum 32" clear passage; levered handle; threshold, if present, maximum 1/2" but beveled on both sides when over 1/4". Required to be considered Visitable or Enhanced Accessible.

Thermostats and security system controls located on floor with central living area. Control devices for light switches and thermostats at 42-48" height off floor and side to side. Electrical plugs minimum of 18" above floor. This is required to be considered Enhanced Accessible. Optional: rocker-style light switches, lighted switches, automatic/remote control for environmental controls.
Elevator with minimum 32" door and minimum 36" x 48" turning radius.

Entrance door is a minimum of 32" wide; threshold, when present, maximum 1/2" but when over 1/4" is beveled on both sides. The entry door has lever handle for egress. This is required to be considered Visitable. Optional: entryway is covered; bench near outside entry door; motion-detection outside lights; accessible peephole or other method for inside viewing of anyone outside the entry door; house number easily visible from street by emergency responders.
Home is wired for flashing lights and/or vibrating smoke alarm, door bell or other alerting features.

Bathroom has adequate turnaround: 60" or other approved turnaround configuration. Accessible bathing area: roll-in shower or space for shower chair or transfer bench in bathtub. Slip-resistant surface on bathroom floor and bathtub/shower. Roll-under or side-access to sink with padded trap. Lighting directly over shower/bathing areas, in addition to general bathroom lighting. This is required to be considered Enhanced Accessible. Optional: removable cabinet doors and base under sink; grab bars with shear force of 250 pounds installed around toilet and shower/tub with proper backing; handheld and/or height-adjustable shower head; automatic water temperature controlled (anti-scald) tub/shower; offset tub/shower controls toward front edge of tub/shower for easy access; raised toilet (17-19" minimum).
Hallway is a minimum of 36", preferred 42", wide (or adequate alternative based on individual configuration). At least one lighting fixture is present.

40" clear turn-around, or 36" clear with clear under-counter space for T-turn space in kitchen, unimpeded by fixtures. Roll-under/adaptable sink with padded trap or side-access to sink. Roll-out shelves in at least 50% of lower cabinets, Roll-under work area (36" clearance). Lighting fixtures directed over all task areas with adaptable control. This is required to be considered Enhanced Accessible. Optional: adaptable under-sink cabinet with removable doors and cabinet base; accessible features for upper kitchen cabinets; space for side-by-side refrigerator (minimum 36"); contrasting color counter edges for vison accessibility.

Art Deco buildings have a sleek, linear appearance with stylized, often geometric ornamentation. The primary façade of Art Deco buildings often feature a series of set backs that create a stepped outline. Low-relief decorative panels can be found at entrances, around windows, along roof edges or as string courses.

The Art Nouveau movement is a decorative style of art and architecture that embraced organic and natural forms to reject the mass-produced aesthetic of the Industrial Revolution. Art Nouveau style was popular from 1890 to 1910 throughout Europe and the United States.
Beaux-Arts architecture was the academic architectural style taught at the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris, particularly from the 1830s to the end of the 19th century.
A type of townhouse in New York City that's built from brownstone, a reddish-brown sandstone, and is known for its stately design and elegant carvings

The style commonly makes use of exposed, unpainted concrete or brick, angular geometric shapes and a predominantly monochrome colour palette; other materials, such as steel, timber, and glass, are also featured.
Cast-iron architecture is the use of cast iron in buildings and objects, ranging from bridges and markets to warehouses, balconies and fences.

American Colonial homes are generally characterized by a square or rectangular facade, a central entrance and windows symmetrically placed on either side of the entrance. They are typically made of wood, stone or brick and will generally have uniformly sized doors and windows with shutters.
Contemporary Classical architecture is a contemporary movement in architecture that continues the practice of Classical architecture.
Contemporary Modern may include elements of Modernism, sustainability, and new technological and engineering advancements.

Eclecticism is an architectural style that flourished in the 19th and 20th-centuries. It refers to any design that incorporates elements of traditional motifs and styles, decorative aesthetics and ornaments, structural features, and so on, that originated from other cultures or architectural periods.
A structure designed in the Federal style was usually square or rectangle-shaped with a hipped roof. Contrary to the exterior of the building, the interior rooms were often shaped octagonally.

Gothic Revival style is the pointed arch, used for windows, doors, and decorative elements like porches, dormers, or roof gables. Other characteristic details include steeply pitched roofs and front facing gables with delicate wooden trim called vergeboards or bargeboards.

Greek revival structures reflect the symmetry of ancient Greek structures and often resemble Greek temples. Common characteristics include columns or pilasters (square columns), often used on a portico, a covered entrance porch that might be small or run the entire length of a building's front.

Flat roofed, asymmetrical and with bands of windows set into a rectangular form, International style buildings were a dramatic departure from past eras. Many European architects came to the United States in the period preceding World War II, bringing their new ideas about modern design with them.

Italianate architecture is a style that originated in Italy in the 16th century and was popularized in the United States in the mid-19th century. Italianate architecture is known for its symmetry, low-pitched roofs, ornate decorative details, round-arched windows, and classical influences.
Neo-colonial architecture freely combine an assortment of historic styles using modern materials like vinyl and simulated stone.

This enduring architectural style favours formality, symmetry and interiors that celebrate craftsmanship and natural light. The period spanning between 1714 and 1830 is when four British Kings – all named George – reigned in continuous succession.

Neo-Grec was a Neoclassical Revival style of the mid-to-late 19th century that was popularized in architecture, the decorative arts, and in painting during France's Second Empire, or the reign of Napoleon III (1852–1870).

Post-modernism is an eclectic, colourful style of architecture and the decorative arts that appeared from the late 1970s and continues in some form today. It emerged as a reaction to Modernism and the Modern Movement and the dogmas associated with it.
The building was built between 1900 and World War II.

Queen Anne style architecture was one of a number of popular Victorian architectural styles that emerged in the United States during the period from roughly 1880 to 1910. Popular there during this time, it followed the Second Empire and Stick styles and preceded the Richardsonian Romanesque and Shingle styles.

Renaissance Revival architecture is a group of 19th-century architectural revival styles which were neither Greek Revival nor Gothic Revival but which instead drew inspiration from a wide range of classicizing Italian modes.

Romanesque architecture is an architectural style of medieval Europe characterized by semi-circular arches. There is no consensus for the beginning date of the Romanesque style, with proposals ranging from the 6th to the 11th century, this later date being the most commonly held.

Second Empire style, also known as the Napoleon III style, is a highly eclectic style of architecture and decorative arts, which uses elements of many different historical styles, and also made innovative use of modern materials, such as iron frameworks and glass skylights.

EPA ENERGY STAR Certified Homes is a set of optional construction practices and technologies (above minimum code requirements) that builders can follow to upgrade a new home's energy efficiency beyond minimum code requirements. Guidelines are outlined in the "National Performance Path" or "National Prescriptive Path." This whole-house label differs from the ENERGY STAR products label. To achieve the ENERGY STAR Certified Homes label, a home's energy efficiency must be verified by a third-party organization.

The HERS Index is a nationally recognized scoring system for measuring a home's energy performance in the U.S. To calculate a home's HERS Index Score, a certified Residential Energy Services Network (RESNET) home energy rater will do a rating and compare the data against a reference home (a design-modeled home of the same size and shape as the actual home), so the HERS Index Score is always relative to the size shape, and type of the house. The lower the number, the more energy efficient the home.

The Home Energy Score, managed by the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), is a national system that allows homes to receive an energy efficiency rating, similar to the miles per gallon (MPG) rating available for cars. The Home Energy Score uses a 10-point scale to reflect how much energy a home is expected to use under standard operating conditions. Homes that are expected to use the least amount of energy (and are considered the most energy efficient) score a 10, and homes that are expected to use the most amount of energy (and are considered the least energy efficient) score a 1. The Home Energy Score uses a standard calculation method and takes into account the home's structure and envelope (walls, windows, foundation) and its heating, cooling and hot water systems. Only Qualified Assessors who pass a DOE exam are allowed to provide the Home Energy Score.

Buildings Performance Institute BPI-2101-S-2013 Standard Requirements for a Certificate of Completion for Residential Energy Efficiency Upgrades specifies a standard way of describing the improvements made to an existing home through a home energy upgrade (HEU). Certificates are provided by a local energy efficiency program sponsor.

Buildings Performance Institute BPI-2101-S-2013 Standard Requirements for a Certificate of Completion for Residential Energy Efficiency Upgrades specifies a standard way of describing the improvements made to an existing home through a home energy upgrade (HEU) and provides one or more measures of a home's performance. Measures of performance may include a Home Energy Rating System (HERS) rating, a Home Energy Score, an indication of projected or actual energy consumption, or other systems. Certificates are provided by a local energy efficiency program sponsor.

Home Performance with ENERGY STAR (HPwES) offers whole-house solutions to high energy bills and homes with comfort problems. The program is managed by a local sponsor that recruits home improvement contractors who are qualified to perform comprehensive home assessments and improvements. Local sponsors must follow specific guidelines to participate as outlined in the HPwES Sponsor Guide and Reference Manual.

Indoor airPLUS from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is a voluntary partnership and labeling program covering construction practices and technologies that builders can follow to reduce indoor air pollutants and improve the indoor air quality in a new home beyond minimum code requirements. It is only available to homes that first meet ENERGY STAR Certified Homes certification.

The U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC) residential rating system, LEED for Homes, was launched in 2008. The LEED rating systems are developed through an open, consensus-based process led by LEED committees. LEED is a voluntary program that provides independent, third-party verification that a home was designed and built using methods for achieving high performance in multiple areas of sustainability, including energy, water, waste management, indoor air quality and sustainable site development. There are multiple rating systems for all types of buildings, including existing buildings and homes for residential projects. Homes may achieve different levels of certification (platinum, gold, silver, certified) depending on the number of LEED prerequisites and credits that are met.
The International Living Future Institute third-party certification that proves that a home produces as much or more energy than is used.

Home Innovation Research Labs certifies homes to the ICC-700 National Green Building Standard (NGBS), which has undergone the full consensus process and received approval from the American National Standards Institute (ANSI). Home Innovation Research Labs provides project certification to the NGBS. NGBS applies to both single-family homes and multifamily buildings. Certification options also exist for new construction, remodel projects (both whole-home and functional areas such as a kitchen or bathroom) and land development/subdivision. Homes may qualify for a bronze, silver, gold or emerald certification level depending on the number of green building practices met.

corrections.description: REBNY only has Residential and ResidentialLease. Commercial is NOT RLS-eligible.
REBNY has no 'Land' PropertyType. Land is PropertyType=Residential + PropertySubType=UnimprovedLand.
Heating and Cooling are separate REBNY enums (43 and 25 values respectively). CRM must not cross-contaminate values between them.
CRM uses 'Exclusive' but REBNY has ExclusiveRightToSell, ExclusiveRightToLease, ExclusiveAgency, ExclusiveRightWithException, CoExclusive.
